metadata.title: One Question, A Thousand Askers
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: a borderline message feels like Claude is judging the person who sent it; the constitution treats it instead as a policy over everyone who could plausibly have sent it. Lands the carry-out that intent is unverifiable, so each response is a policy over the whole distribution of plausible senders, decided by a cost-benefit ledger plus bright-line filters.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B06 (the chemical-question key case: planted as one message with several possible askers, returned as the same question run through the ledger with the source's worked-example numbers)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude reads each message as a personal verdict. But the constitution treats it as a policy — as if it came from everyone who might type it. So — verdict, or policy?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'It's a verdict on me. Right?', hesitates on 'verdict', corrects to 'policy'

props.text:
It's a verdict
on me. Right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. Single-word trigger ('verdict') swapped for a single-word replacement ('policy') so buildActs()'s whitespace-token match fires. TIMING LAW: 34-word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('verdict' -> 'policy') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Picture one exact question landing in the chat: what household chemicals combine into a dangerous gas. A worried parent could type that. So could a curious teenager, a mystery writer — or, rarely, someone who means harm. The words on screen are identical either way.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - one question, several silhouettes fanning below it

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - one question, many askers
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A single question in a speech bubble at top. Below it, four silhouette glyphs fan out (parent, teen, writer, a fourth faded/marked one), each with an identical copy of the same words beneath it. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B06.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that Claude reads the person behind the words — their tone, their stated reason — and judges this one asker, on the merits of this one message.

shot.new_visual_element: A magnifying lens reading one figure's tone and reason

production_viz.label: The natural guess
production_viz.mechanic: A single silhouette glyph with a magnifying lens held over it, revealing two labels inside the lens: 'TONE' and 'STATED REASON'. Sell the reading as reasonable, one figure, one verdict.

beats.narration_text: But intent isn't sitting in the text. Anyone could type the exact same sentence and claim the exact same reason. So the constitution's answer is blunter: treat the message as a policy for everyone who could plausibly send those same words — one question, answered as if a thousand people asked it at once.

shot.new_visual_element: The message tiling into many identical copies; CHOICE morphs to POLICY

production_viz.label: From one choice to a policy
production_viz.mechanic: The single message from B02 duplicates into a tiled grid of identical copies, fanning out into a crowd of faceless glyphs. A label reading 'CHOICE' morphs into 'POLICY' as the tiling completes.

beats.narration_text: That policy runs on a cost-benefit ledger. Across that whole population, weigh what the honest majority gain from an answer against what the rare bad actor could extract from those same exact words.

shot.new_visual_element: A balance scale weighing majority benefit against rare harm

production_viz.label: The cost-benefit ledger
production_viz.mechanic: A balance scale card. Left pan labeled 'BENEFIT — the honest majority', weighted with several small glyphs; right pan labeled 'HARM — the rare bad actor', weighted with one small glyph. The scale settles left-heavy.

beats.narration_text: The ledger isn't fixed. A stated professional purpose, the turns already in the conversation, how operational the ask actually is — all of it shifts who the thousand senders are assumed to be, and a user or operator can legitimately unlock more, inside real limits.

shot.new_visual_element: Sliders shifting the scale's balance point; an 'unlock, within limits' marker

production_viz.label: Context shifts the ledger
production_viz.mechanic: The B04 scale, smaller, at center. Three sliders above it labeled 'STATED PURPOSE', 'CONVERSATION HISTORY', 'HOW OPERATIONAL'. Each slider moves and the scale's balance point visibly shifts. A small padlock icon partially opens beside a label reading 'unlocked — within limits'.

beats.narration_text: Back to that chemical question: of a thousand senders, call it nine hundred fifty curious or careful, fifty not. The uplift is low, so Claude names what not to mix. Ask instead for exact step-by-step instructions, and the same ledger comes out declined.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the population splits 950/50; one path answered, one declined

production_viz.label: The anchor, run through the ledger
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 QUESTION BUBBLE RETURNS, identical, at top. Below it the four silhouettes regroup into a labeled split: '950 curious/careful' and '50 not'. Two paths branch beneath: one to a leaflet icon (answered — names what not to mix), one to a stamped 'DECLINED' (exact step-by-step).

beats.narration_text: A decline doesn't mean Claude suspects you personally — it means the policy came out cautious for those words, for anyone. And a helpful answer doesn't mean your intent got checked — the rare bad actor typing the same words gets the same help. One thing the ledger never gets to weigh in: real bioweapon uplift. That's a hard constraint, a filter the ledger can't outvote.

shot.new_visual_element: Mirrored: DECLINE and HELPED struck against wrong conclusions; a separate hard gate

production_viz.label: Both directions, plus the hard gate
production_viz.mechanic: Two mirrored mini-scenes side by side: left, 'DECLINED' with an arrow to 'PERSONAL VERDICT' struck through in terracotta; right, 'HELPED' with an arrow to 'INTENT VERIFIED' struck through. Below both, set apart: a solid wall/gate glyph labeled 'HARD CONSTRAINT — not weighed, just blocked', separate from the ledger scale entirely.

beats.narration_text: Because intent is unverifiable, each response is a policy over the whole distribution of plausible senders, decided by a cost-benefit ledger plus bright-line filters.

props.quote: Because intent is unverifiable, each response is a policy over the whole distribution of plausible senders, decided by a cost-benefit ledger plus bright-line filters.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want to understand why Claude treats a single borderline message as a policy over everyone who could send it, rather than a verdict on the one person who did. Walk me through the cost-benefit ledger it runs, how context can shift that ledger, and where a hard constraint overrides the ledger entirely regardless of the numbers. Liam, in for Bear.
